items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I remember going to a John Cage concert

ctx.x: Oh fabulous. And again, here you have, there’s a predictable aspect. I don’t mean this as any kind of criticism, this is merely an observation from thinking about the stage of the Half Note in New York where the piano was always facing one of the walls and the band was behind you. So you never saw anybody in the band unless you turned around. So you

never had the distraction of anything that was happening visually, so you just listened for all that time. So there was a kind of a straight-aheadness and predictability about where Clark would go, and a totally unpredictable aspect of Brookmeyer. So along with the other scenarios that I’ve given you, I was in the cage at the time, I was also into a marriage with a woman that absolutely detested everything twentieth century and really made my life miserable, so I got deeply into twentieth century music, to the…
Did the audience go with you?
